chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from al-Husayn ibn Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'I forget the recitation in the first rak'ah.' He said, 'Recite in the second.' I said, 'I forget in the second.' He said, 'Recite in the third.' I said, 'I forget in all my prayers.' He said, 'When you remember the bowing and prostration, your prayer is complete.'

His saying (peace be upon him), 'If you miss it in the first, then recite in the second,' did not mean that he intended to repeat the recitation of what had missed in the first, but rather he intended to recite in the second and third what is specific to them from the recitation; as for the first, its ruling has passed. The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: 'If he leaves the bowing, whether forgetfully or deliberately, he must repeat.' This is indicated by what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I forget to recite the Quran in the first rak'ah of my prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that forgetting recitation is a minor omission that does not break the prayer's validity, instructing the worshipper to simply proceed rather than restart. The text further distinguishes this from missing a pillar like *ruku'*, which necessitates repetition, highlighting the Shia juristic principle that only the omission of essential pillars invalidates the prayer. This ruling underscores the practical ease (*taysir*) granted to believers in daily worship, ensuring that minor lapses in memory do not burden the faithful with excessive re-performance.
